description:
The nls_panel.gdt dataset (National Longitudinal Survey panel of 716 young women observed over multiple years) is loaded in Gretl. Variables include: 'lwage' (log wage), 'educ' (education), 'exper' (experience), 'expersq' (experience squared), 'black' (=1 if Black), 'south' (=1 if South), 'union' (=1 if union member), 'tenure' (job tenure).

A labor economist must determine whether to use Fixed Effects (FE) or Random Effects (RE) panel estimation. Your task:
1. Estimate a Pooled OLS model: lwage ~ educ + exper + expersq + black + south + union
2. Estimate a Fixed Effects (within estimator) model with the same specification
3. Estimate a Random Effects (GLS) model with the same specification
4. Run the Hausman specification test to determine which estimator (FE or RE) is consistent
5. Interpret the Hausman test result and report which estimator is preferred
6. Save all results (all three models + Hausman test) to /home/ga/Documents/gretl_output/panel_results.txt

Gretl is open with nls_panel.gdt loaded as a panel dataset.

metadata.data_source: National Longitudinal Survey (NLS) of Young Women, POE5 sample
